extracted.intended_audience: MIT and Lincoln Laboratory researchers/inventors submitting invention disclosures to the Technology Ventures Office / Technology Licensing Office
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and form-level requirements for submitting an invention disclosure to MIT Lincoln Laboratory's Technology Ventures Office/TLO, including what to report, definitions (conception, reduction to practice, publication), funding and inventor-identification rules, and signature/assignment obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission trigger (what to disclose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit when something new, non-obvious, and useful has been conceived or developed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The purpose of this form is to notify the MIT TLO of your potential invention and any relevant sponsorship and publication history. The form also serves to establish a legal record of the date of conception of the invention. This form and supporting attachments should be submitted via the Lincoln Laboratory Technology Ventures Office (TVO) at IPdisclosures@ll.mit.edu. Refer to TVO-052, Intellectual Property Management for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a brief descriptive title
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a brief descriptive title to aid in identifying the technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of the technology (required content)
rubrics_metrics.description: In describing the technology, select the check box and attach material that covers the following points: a. General purpose; b. Technical description; c. Advantages and improvements over existing methods, devices or materials; d. Commercial applications (economic potential, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check here to confirm a description of the technology is attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: List all inventors and identify MIT vs non-MIT inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the check box and attach a list of the name(s) of any MIT co-inventors. An MIT co-inventor is anyone affiliated with or employed by MIT who has conceived or contributed an essential element of the invention, either independently or jointly with others, during the evolution of the technology concept or reduction to practice. Non-MIT co-inventors are individuals who conceived or contributed an essential invention element and are affiliated with or employed by any entity other than MIT or Lincoln Laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include employer/institution affiliation, email, phone number. If there are more than four MIT inventors, attach additional copies of the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify all funding sources (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: For this step all funding sources need to be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate and complete grant and contract information is necessary; the MIT TLO will use this information to determine any sponsor rights and to comply with all requirements under sponsored research agreements and federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIT-administered funding disclosure (4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Was this invention developed with the use of MIT-administered research grant/contract funds? YES applies under either of the following two circumstances: (1) If the invention was supported by any on-contract funding (most Lab programs), select YES and then select the check box for MIT LL Prime Contract number (FA8702-15-D-0001). (2) If the software was supported by off-contract funding, such as a Cooperative Research and Development Agreement (CRADA), Collaboration Agreement (CA), or Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR), select YES, then select the OTHER check box and provide the applicable agreement number(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For both of the above options, you need to enter the Program number, Sponsor/Organization, and Lab Program Manager. Program numbers and the sponsor/organization name or acronym may be obtained from the appropriate group or division office. The Laboratory program manager is generally the cognizant group leader. Refer any questions to the Technology Ventures Office (TVO) at IPdisclosures@ll.mit.edu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant use of MIT-administered funds or facilities (even if NO)
rubrics_metrics.description: If NO MIT administered research grants/contract funds were used, you must still report on whether the invention was developed with significant use of any MIT-administered funds or facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in the absence of program funding, significant use will normally give rise to MIT ownership rights in the invention. For more information on what is meant by 'Significant Use' refer to § 2.1.2 of the Guide to the Ownership, Distribution and Commercial Development of MIT Technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-MIT funding disclosure (4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-MIT inventors are also asked to disclose their funding sources outside of MIT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is necessary to confirm sponsor rights, joint ownership, and (as appropriate) to establish inter-agency agreement(s) to manage the intellectual property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure and foreign/US filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: In the United States, a patent application must be filed no later than one year after public availability of a printed publication disclosing the invention in detail. Once the filing deadline has passed, USPTO regulations prevent the invention from being patented. In other countries, filing must take place before either oral or printed publication is made available to the public or foreign filing rights may be forfeited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presentations including slides, use of overheads, blackboards, or website postings may be considered written disclosures. However, where there has been a U.S. filing before any oral or printed publication, a one-year grace period for foreign filing is generally granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions: Conception, First Publication, First Public Oral Disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Conception involves the formulation, in the mind of the inventor, of the complete means for solving a problem; mere recognition of a desirable result or a general approach is insufficient. b. 'First Publication' means the first time any member of the general public (those outside the MIT community), without restriction of confidentiality, would have been able to legally gain access to your written or printed enabling description of the invention. c. 'First public oral disclosure' means the first time any member of the general public... would have heard a presentation or other oral disclosure of the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates of conception, publication, oral disclosure, and anticipated publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the Date of Conception of Invention (and where documented), First Publication (including publication and submission date), First Public Oral Disclosure, and Anticipated Date of Publication if unpublished and undisclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate data is essential, as prior disclosure may affect the possibility of obtaining patent rights. If unpublished and undisclosed, provide the anticipated publication or public oral disclosure date and any submissions made for potential publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to practice (yes/no and definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select either the YES or NO check box. Reduction to practice, according to patent law, involves actual and complete use of the invention for its intended purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such reduction to practice generally involves physical construction of the invention and testing the physical embodiment to determine whether it performs as contemplated, but this is not always necessary if the invention can be fully described. If YES, provide date of first reduction to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: List potential commercial entities/contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of commercial entities that may be interested in the invention will assist the MIT TLO in identifying potential licensees for the technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please include names and emails of specific contacts (if known). Check here to confirm a list is attached of commercial entities that may be interested in this invention (include company name, points of contacts, and emails).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary contact declaration and accuracy of information
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary contact signs to agree that all supplied information is true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I hereby declare that the details furnished above are true and correct to the best of my knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and cooperation obligation for MIT inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: For MIT inventors: I (we) hereby assign all right, title and interest to this invention to MIT and agree to execute all documents as requested, assigning to MIT our rights in any patent application filed on this invention, and to cooperate with the MIT Technology Licensing Office (the 'TLO') in the protection of this invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MIT will share any royalty income derived from the invention with the inventor(s) according to its standard policies, as may be updated from time to time. The signature of non-MIT inventors without MIT ID numbers is not required; they will be contacted by the MIT TLO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal and contact information required (identifiers and correspondence preferences)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide first/middle/last name, home address, city, state, zip, MIT ID#, country of citizenship, birth month/day (MIT collects month/day rather than SSNs for security), email, and indicate whether you wish to be copied on Patent Office and related correspondence (YES/NO).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information, as well as home address and country of citizenship, is required. Absence of this information may hinder distribution of the inventors’ share of any royalties that may result from this technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: References/comments (presentations/publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please include conference name(s) and presentation title(s) and date(s); use separate sheet if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission pathway and assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all sections are complete, including approval signatures, submit to the TVO at IPdisclosures@ll.mit.edu. All MIT inventors must sign the disclosure before it is submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer any questions to the Technology Ventures Office (TVO) at IPdisclosures@ll.mit.edu.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of grant/contract info to determine sponsor rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that accurate and complete grant and contract information is necessary. The MIT TLO will use this information to determine any sponsor rights and to comply with all requirements under sponsored research agreements and federal law.
